quote.text: I left something half finished and lost where I was

promise.text: How to restart a project you gave up on

art.why: the carousel's topic: the moment and its guide name "restart", "half finished"

lines.text: Coming back costs more than starting did, mostly the rebuilding of where you got to.
What to write down, and how to resume without re-reading everything.

head.text: Put out what you already have.

body.text: The form, the emails, the receipt, whatever you did last time, all where you can see it.

head.text: Write where you got to, in one line.

body.text: Where you stopped inside the task, not what the task is.
If you can't tell, look for the newest thing you produced: the last email sent, the last page filled in.

head.text: Check whether it still needs doing.

body.text: Ask three questions: is anyone waiting on it, does it have a date that has passed or is coming, and would you be glad to have it done?

head.text: Look for what was missing last time.

body.text: A password, a document that never arrived, an answer someone else owed you.
If it's still missing, getting it is your real next step, and it's often a short call or email.

head.text: Name the smallest piece and do only that.

body.text: Small enough that starting it isn't a decision: find the paperwork and put it on the desk, photograph one sticker, write the first line of the email.

line.text: It remembers exactly where you got to, so picking it back up is not starting over.
